speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting, I need to know if you have passed meconium stool and when your first bowel movement occurred. Please also tell me if there is any family history of intestinal atresia or Hirschsprung's disease.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. Given the classic presentation of bilious vomiting in a newborn with a sibling history of pyloric stenosis, the most likely cause is a congenital obstruction such as duodenal atresia. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray
